article.story: MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- — Drake Maye threw two touchdown passes and rushed for a score as the New England Patriots came back to beat the Miami Dolphins 24-19 on Sunday. With star receiver AJ Brown inactive because of lingering injuries, Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and the Patriots (5-3) rallied from a 10-point halftime deficit to take a 17-13 lead entering the fourth, then held on after a late Miami rally. DeMario Douglas caught a pass and weaved through the Dolphins secondary for a 48-yard touchdown catch that put the Patriots up two scores early in the fourth. The Patriots hadn’t had a clean operation in the first half, but they took advantage of the young Dolphins’ mistakes in the second, outscoring Miami 21-0 until Malik Willis threw a 35-yard touchdown to rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. with two minutes left. After an unsuccessful two-point try by Miami, Stevenson recovered Bradley Pinion's onside kick, and New England kept the ball from there. Stevenson had 19 carries for 82 yards, and Douglas caught three passes for 76 yards. One week after leading Miami (1-6) to its first win of the season, Willis completed 21 of 32 passes for 211 yards. He threw for two touchdowns and had an interception while being sacked five times. The Patriots pulled within three when Maye lofted a pass to Kyle Williams for a 43-yard touchdown that was initially ruled an incompletion after Williams' knee appeared to jar the ball loose. When coach Mike Vrabel demonstratively launched the red challenge flag, officials overturned the call to a touchdown after replays showed Williams crossed the goal line before losing possession of the ball. Miami went three-and-out on the next drive, its momentum stalled after Ollie Gordon drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after saying something to a defender following a 5-yard carry. Coach Jeff Hafley removed Gordon from the game for a play, and the second-year running back appeared visibly upset on the sideline. Maye faked a pitch to Rhamondre Stevenson and ran it in for the 2-yard go-ahead score with 59 seconds left in the third — his fifth straight game with at least three total touchdowns. Willis led the Dolphins on an 11-play, 70-yard two-minute drive that Malik Washington capped a 1-yard touchdown to put Miami ahead 13-3 at the half. Washington had briefly left the game after taking a hard hit from Patriots linebacker Christian Elliss earlier in the drive. Elliss was flagged for unnecessary roughness for the hit, and Washington, after a brief trip to the blue medial tent, returned five plays later to catch his first receiving touchdown of the season. Zane Gonzalez, in his second game since re-signing with Miami, hit field goals of 31 and 52 yards, the latter of which doinked off the left upright and through. He missed a 43-yard attempt in the fourth. Injuries Patriots: TE Hunter Henry (foot) left in the second quarter and did not return. ... Linebacker Gabe Jacas (knee) left in the third and didn't return. Dolphins: Edge rusher Malik Herring left in the second with a stringer but in the third. Up next Patriots: Host Green Bay next Sunday. Dolphins: Host Detroit next Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
